title: AlphaFold-Multimer predicts 2,895 interactions among human mitochondrial proteins
summary: Texas A&M AgriLife Research screened 630,003 protein pairs from about 1,100 human mitochondrial proteins with AlphaFold-Multimer and identified 2,895 likely interactions, more than half not previously reported, giving 85 uncharacterized proteins their first probable partners. The paper appeared in Nature Communications on 25 August 2026 and the institutional release on 5 November. Lab experiments in yeast and human cells confirmed several of the partnerships; most predictions remain untested, and the disease links are potential targets, not established ones. Predictions are shared through the MitoMatch web tool.
organization: Texas A&M AgriLife Research; and Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis

evidence.tested: AlphaFold-Multimer screened about 630,000 protein pairs; lab experiments in yeast and human cells confirmed several of the predicted partnerships, while the release does not say how many of the 2,895 were tested.
evidence.unknown: Only several predictions were confirmed, most remain unverified, the interactions are described as likely rather than established, and disease links are potential targets.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold-Multimer predicted pairwise interactions among mitochondrial proteins; the predictions were released as the MitoMatch web resource.
